messages:
support-ops: Customers (multiple tenants) reporting high p99 API latency and intermittent TLS handshake failures for requests originating from EU regions to our hosted endpoints. Spike started ~2026-03-16 11:14 UTC, p99 ~ 2.8s -> 7.1s. Errors: CONNECT_TIMEOUT / tls: handshake failure. Seen in eu-west and eu-central. :warning:

jon (oncall): Copy — can you paste a couple of request_ids + probe ids and any traceroutes you have? I’ll check routing tables and recent route changes.

support-ops: request_ids: r-9f3b2a, r-9f3b56. probe ids: probe-eu-12, probe-eu-21. Quick traceroute from probe-eu-12: ```traceroute to api.redwood.example (52.14.22.7), 30 hops max
 1 10.0.3.1 0.6 ms
 2 203.0.113.5 1.2 ms
 3 198.51.100.2 5.4 ms
 4 198.51.100.33 8.9 ms
 5 203.0.113.75 120.4 ms 
 6 198.51.200.12 125.1 ms
 7 52.14.22.7 126.2 ms
``` note the big jump at hop 5 -> likely hairpin into APAC.

maria (eng-sre): Interesting — hop 5 looks like a peering change. Any recent GSLB weight adjustments or DNS TTLs changed?

support-ops: We rolled a DNS weight tweak at 10:50 UTC for a subset of eu queries to shift traffic during scheduled maintenance. TTL was temporarily lowered to 20s.

jon (oncall): That matches the timing. Lower TTL + weight tweak could expose transient BGP/peering asymmetry causing hairpinning to APAC POPs. For quick mitigation: revert the weight change and restore TTL to 300s. Can someone rollback the GSLB weight now? @deploy-bot any blockers? :eyes: 

deploy-bot: Rolling rollback of GSLB weight for eu pool -> previous weights restored. Change ID: chg-20260316-44. Propagating to authoritative DNS.

sre-bot: Alert suppressed for affected routes. Noting correlation between GSLB change and spike.

maria (eng-sre): While DNS is converging, we should also enable fallback routing to local eu dedicated pool to avoid TLS hairpin. Steps: 1) add route override for eu prefix group to prefer eu-dedicated-backend for 30m; 2) increase TLS handshake timeout on edge from 2s -> 6s for impacted frontends. I can patch the routing policy and TLS config if you OK.

jon (oncall): Do it. Also capture tcpdump for one of the affected frontends (frontend-eu-02) for 5 minutes and save to /tmp/ for postmortem. Command: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/eu-front-eu02-0316.pcap port 443 and host 52.14.22.7`

maria (eng-sre): On it. Applying route override + TLS timeout bump now. Will open change chg-20260316-45 for the temporary override.

support-ops: Noted a visible drop in errors ~45s after rollback and config changes, p99 trending back to ~2.2s. Customers reporting fewer timeouts. :white_check_mark:

jon (oncall): Good. Next actions for follow-up: - postmortem including DNS TTL change rationale; - verify peering with carrier at hop 5 (contact network vendor) - add automated check that flags large geo egress hops (eu -> non-eu) in traceroutes after any GSLB weight changes.

maria (eng-sre): Agreed. I’ll collect tcpdump + app logs + routing table snapshot and upload to the incident bucket (s3://redwood-incident/6032104567/). Will also revert the temporary TLS timeout after stabilization.

support-ops: Thanks — I’ll update affected customers with mitigation summary and ETA for postmortem.

jon (oncall): Marking thread resolved for now, moving to follow-up. :handshake:
